第 4 步：实现数据模型和存储库 (Repository)

创建 src/main/java/com/example/security/domain/SecurityAlert.java：

package com.example.security.domain;

import jakarta.persistence.Column;
import jakarta.persistence.Entity;
import jakarta.persistence.GeneratedValue;
import jakarta.persistence.GenerationType;
import jakarta.persistence.Id;
import jakarta.persistence.Table;

import java.time.Instant;

@Entity
@Table(name = "security_alert")
public class SecurityAlert {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    @Column(name = "tenant_id", nullable = false)
    private String tenantId;

    @Column(nullable = false)
    private String severity;

    @Column(nullable = false)
    private String status;

    @Column(name = "source_ip")
    private String sourceIp;

    @Column(name = "asset_id")
    private String assetId;

    @Column(name = "detected_at", nullable = false)
    private Instant detectedAt;

    @Column(name = "updated_at", nullable = false)
    private Instant updatedAt;

    protected SecurityAlert() {
    }

    public Long getId() {
        return id;
    }

    public String getTenantId() {
        return tenantId;
    }

    public String getSeverity() {
        return severity;
    }

    public String getStatus() {
        return status;
    }

    public String getSourceIp() {
        return sourceIp;
    }

    public String getAssetId() {
        return assetId;
    }

    public Instant getDetectedAt() {
        return detectedAt;
    }

    public Instant getUpdatedAt() {
        return updatedAt;
    }
}

创建 src/main/java/com/example/security/repository/SeverityCount.java：

package com.example.security.repository;

public interface SeverityCount {
    String getSeverity();
    Long getTotal();
}

创建 src/main/java/com/example/security/repository/SecurityAlertRepository.java：

package com.example.security.repository;

import com.example.security.domain.SecurityAlert;
import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository;
import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.Query;
import org.springframework.data.repository.query.Param;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;

public interface SecurityAlertRepository extends JpaRepository<SecurityAlert, Long> {

    @Query(value = """
        SELECT severity AS severity, COUNT(*) AS total
        FROM security_alert
        WHERE tenant_id = :tenantId
          AND detected_at >= :fromTime
        GROUP BY severity
        """, nativeQuery = true)
    List<SeverityCount> countBySeverity(
        @Param("tenantId") String tenantId,
        @Param("fromTime") Instant fromTime
    );

    @Query(value = """
        SELECT COUNT(*)
        FROM security_alert
        WHERE tenant_id = :tenantId
          AND status = 'OPEN'
          AND detected_at >= :fromTime
        """, nativeQuery = true)
    long countOpenAlerts(
        @Param("tenantId") String tenantId,
        @Param("fromTime") Instant fromTime
    );
}

存储库在 PostgreSQL 中执行聚合，而不是将所有告警加载到应用程序内存中。即使在本地机器上，这也很重要，因为实现应保持正确的计算边界。PostgreSQL 对行进行计数和分组，而应用程序将紧凑的结果转换为 API 响应。

创建 src/main/java/com/example/security/dto/AlertSummary.java：

package com.example.security.dto;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.Map;

public record AlertSummary(
    String tenantId,
    Instant windowStart,
    Instant generatedAt,
    long totalAlerts,
    long openAlerts,
    Map<String, Long> bySeverity,
    String deliverySource
) {
    public AlertSummary withDeliverySource(String source) {
        return new AlertSummary(
            tenantId,
            windowStart,
            generatedAt,
            totalAlerts,
            openAlerts,
            bySeverity,
            source
        );
    }
}

deliverySource 值使本地行为可视化。响应可以标识它是否来自 Redis、实时聚合还是定时刷新逻辑。在更大的系统中，响应包络还可以包括缓存年龄、数据源水位线 (watermark) 和计算版本。

第 5 步：配置 Redis 序列化

创建 src/main/java/com/example/security/config/RedisConfig.java：

package com.example.security.config;

import com.example.security.dto.AlertSummary;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.RedisConnectionFactory;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.RedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.data.redis.serializer.Jackson2JsonRedisSerializer;
import org.springframework.data.redis.serializer.StringRedisSerializer;

@Configuration
public class RedisConfig {

    @Bean
    RedisTemplate<String, AlertSummary> alertSummaryRedisTemplate(
        RedisConnectionFactory connectionFactory,
        ObjectMapper objectMapper
    ) {
        RedisTemplate<String, AlertSummary> template = new RedisTemplate<>();
        template.setConnectionFactory(connectionFactory);

        Jackson2JsonRedisSerializer<AlertSummary> valueSerializer =
            new Jackson2JsonRedisSerializer<>(objectMapper, AlertSummary.class);

        template.setKeySerializer(new StringRedisSerializer());
        template.setValueSerializer(valueSerializer);
        template.setHashKeySerializer(new StringRedisSerializer());
        template.setHashValueSerializer(valueSerializer);
        template.afterPropertiesSet();
        return template;
    }
}

显式序列化可保持 Redis 值具备可读性，并避免依赖 Java 原生序列化。键序列化器存储纯字符串键，值序列化器将摘要存储为 JSON。

第 6 步：实现实时聚合

创建 src/main/java/com/example/security/service/AlertAggregationService.java：

package com.example.security.service;

import com.example.security.dto.AlertSummary;
import com.example.security.repository.SecurityAlertRepository;
import com.example.security.repository.SeverityCount;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

@Service
public class AlertAggregationService {

    private final SecurityAlertRepository repository;
    private final Clock clock;
    private final long windowHours;

    public AlertAggregationService(
        SecurityAlertRepository repository,
        @Value("${app.summary.window-hours}") long windowHours
    ) {
        this(repository, Clock.systemUTC(), windowHours);
    }

    AlertAggregationService(
        SecurityAlertRepository repository,
        Clock clock,
        long windowHours
    ) {
        this.repository = repository;
        this.clock = clock;
        this.windowHours = windowHours;
    }

    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    public AlertSummary aggregate(String tenantId, String source) {
        Instant generatedAt = clock.instant();
        Instant windowStart = generatedAt.minus(windowHours, ChronoUnit.HOURS);

        List<SeverityCount> rows = repository.countBySeverity(tenantId, windowStart);
        long openAlerts = repository.countOpenAlerts(tenantId, windowStart);

        Map<String, Long> bySeverity = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        bySeverity.put("CRITICAL", 0L);
        bySeverity.put("HIGH", 0L);
        bySeverity.put("MEDIUM", 0L);
        bySeverity.put("LOW", 0L);

        for (SeverityCount row : rows) {
            bySeverity.put(row.getSeverity(), row.getTotal());
        }

        long totalAlerts = bySeverity.values()
            .stream()
            .mapToLong(Long::longValue)
            .sum();

        return new AlertSummary(
            tenantId,
            windowStart,
            generatedAt,
            totalAlerts,
            openAlerts,
            Map.copyOf(bySeverity),
            source
        );
    }
}

该服务是权威的计算路径。它既被定时处理使用，也被缓存未命中恢复使用。保持单一的聚合实现可防止定时和按需响应偏离一致的业务定义。

计算使用 UTC 时钟和显式的 24 小时窗口。对于确定性的单元测试，包私有（package-private）的构造函数接收一个固定的时钟。

第 7 步：实现 Redis 读取、写入和回填行为

创建 src/main/java/com/example/security/service/AlertSummaryCache.java：

package com.example.security.service;

import com.example.security.dto.AlertSummary;
import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.data.redis.RedisConnectionFailureException;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.RedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.Optional;

@Service
public class AlertSummaryCache {

    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(AlertSummaryCache.class);

    private final RedisTemplate<String, AlertSummary> redisTemplate;
    private final String keyPrefix;
    private final Duration ttl;

    public AlertSummaryCache(
        RedisTemplate<String, AlertSummary> redisTemplate,
        @Value("${app.summary.cache-prefix}") String keyPrefix,
        @Value("${app.summary.cache-ttl}") Duration ttl
    ) {
        this.redisTemplate = redisTemplate;
        this.keyPrefix = keyPrefix;
        this.ttl = ttl;
    }

    public Optional<AlertSummary> get(String tenantId) {
        try {
            return Optional.ofNullable(redisTemplate.opsForValue().get(key(tenantId)));
        } catch (RedisConnectionFailureException ex) {
            log.warn("Redis read failed for tenant {}; continuing without cache", tenantId);
            return Optional.empty();
        }
    }

    public void put(String tenantId, AlertSummary summary) {
        try {
            redisTemplate.opsForValue().set(key(tenantId), summary, ttl);
        } catch (RedisConnectionFailureException ex) {
            log.warn("Redis write failed for tenant {}; response remains available", tenantId);
        }
    }

    public void evict(String tenantId) {
        try {
            redisTemplate.delete(key(tenantId));
        } catch (RedisConnectionFailureException ex) {
            log.warn("Redis eviction failed for tenant {}", tenantId);
        }
    }

    public String key(String tenantId) {
        return keyPrefix + ":tenant:" + tenantId + ":window:24h";
    }
}

该缓存包装器将 Redis 视为加速层，而不是记录的来源（source of record）。Redis 连接失败会变成一次缓存未命中，而不是导致请求立即失败。应用程序仍可以从 PostgreSQL 聚合数据。如果回填写入失败，当前响应仍然可用，尽管后续请求需要再次聚合，直到 Redis 恢复。

创建 src/main/java/com/example/security/service/AlertSummaryService.java：

package com.example.security.service;

import com.example.security.dto.AlertSummary;
import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
import java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock;

@Service
public class AlertSummaryService {

    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(AlertSummaryService.class);

    private final AlertSummaryCache cache;
    private final AlertAggregationService aggregationService;
    private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, ReentrantLock> localLocks = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    public AlertSummaryService(
        AlertSummaryCache cache,
        AlertAggregationService aggregationService
    ) {
        this.cache = cache;
        this.aggregationService = aggregationService;
    }

    public AlertSummary getSummary(String tenantId) {
        return cache.get(tenantId)
            .map(summary -> summary.withDeliverySource("CACHE"))
            .orElseGet(() -> aggregateAndBackfill(tenantId));
    }

    public AlertSummary refresh(String tenantId, String source) {
        AlertSummary summary = aggregationService.aggregate(tenantId, source);
        cache.put(tenantId, summary);
        return summary;
    }

    public void evict(String tenantId) {
        cache.evict(tenantId);
    }

    private AlertSummary aggregateAndBackfill(String tenantId) {
        ReentrantLock lock = localLocks.computeIfAbsent(tenantId, ignored -> new ReentrantLock());
        lock.lock();
        try {
            return cache.get(tenantId)
                .map(summary -> summary.withDeliverySource("CACHE_AFTER_WAIT"))
                .orElseGet(() -> {
                    log.info("Cache miss for tenant {}; running real-time aggregation", tenantId);
                    return refresh(tenantId, "REAL_TIME_BACKFILL");
                });
        } finally {
            lock.unlock();
            if (!lock.hasQueuedThreads()) {
                localLocks.remove(tenantId, lock);
            }
        }
    }
}

服务首先读取 Redis。如果在未命中的情况下，它将获取每个租户级别的本地锁，再次检查 Redis，仅当键仍不存在时才执行实时聚合，然后再回填 Redis。

第二次缓存检查很重要。多个并发请求可能会观察到相同的初始未命中。第一个请求计算并写入值。排队等待锁的请求随后会再次检查 Redis 并重用该结果，而不是重复进行数据库聚合（防缓存击穿）。

这种本地锁适用于单个本地应用程序进程。如果启动了多个应用程序实例，每个进程都有自己的锁。在更大规模的系统中，将需要分布式锁或基于 Redis 的 single-flight 机制来跨实例协调缓存未命中。该扩展特意排除在此本地设置之外。

第 8 步：实现定时缓存刷新

创建 src/main/java/com/example/security/service/AlertSummaryScheduler.java：

package com.example.security.service;

import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.scheduling.annotation.Scheduled;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.List;

@Component
public class AlertSummaryScheduler {

    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(AlertSummaryScheduler.class);

    private final AlertSummaryService summaryService;
    private final List<String> tenants;

    public AlertSummaryScheduler(
        AlertSummaryService summaryService,
        @Value("${app.summary.tenants}") List<String> tenants
    ) {
        this.summaryService = summaryService;
        this.tenants = List.copyOf(tenants);
    }

    @Scheduled(
        initialDelayString = "10000",
        fixedDelayString = "${app.summary.schedule-delay-ms}"
    )
    public void refreshConfiguredTenants() {
        for (String tenantId : tenants) {
            try {
                summaryService.refresh(tenantId, "SCHEDULED_REFRESH");
                log.info("Scheduled summary refresh completed for tenant {}", tenantId);
            } catch (Exception ex) {
                log.error("Scheduled summary refresh failed for tenant {}", tenantId, ex);
            }
        }
    }
}

调度器在应用程序启动后等待 10 秒，然后刷新每个配置的租户。它在上一次执行完成 5 分钟后再运行。fixedDelay 可以避免在前一个方法仍在执行时就启动新的本地运行。

单个租户的失败会在循环内部被捕获，以便剩余的租户仍能被刷新。定时执行和实时未命中恢复使用同一个 refresh 方法，因此使用相同的聚合定义和缓存格式。

package com.example.security.controller;

import com.example.security.dto.AlertSummary;
import com.example.security.service.AlertSummaryService;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.validation.annotation.Validated;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.DeleteMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@Validated
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/alert-summary")
public class AlertSummaryController {

    private final AlertSummaryService summaryService;

    public AlertSummaryController(AlertSummaryService summaryService) {
        this.summaryService = summaryService;
    }

    @GetMapping
    public AlertSummary getSummary(
        @PathVariable
        @Pattern(regexp = "[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,64}")
        String tenantId
    ) {
        return summaryService.getSummary(tenantId);
    }

    @PostMapping("/refresh")
    public AlertSummary refresh(
        @PathVariable
        @Pattern(regexp = "[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,64}")
        String tenantId
    ) {
        return summaryService.refresh(tenantId, "MANUAL_REFRESH");
    }

    @DeleteMapping("/cache")
    public ResponseEntity<Void> evict(
        @PathVariable
        @Pattern(regexp = "[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,64}")
        String tenantId
    ) {
        summaryService.evict(tenantId);

    }
}

GET 路由演示了正常的三层交付路径。POST 路由强制立即聚合数据并覆盖缓存的摘要。DELETE 路由移除某个租户的键，以便下一个 GET 请求能够演示实时聚合和回填过程。

这些刷新和逐出路由属于本地开发实用工具。在共享或生产环境中，未经身份验证和授权，不应将其暴露。

第 13 步：验证 Redis 故障降级 (Fallback)

仅停止 Redis 容器：

docker compose stop redis

调用摘要端点：

curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/v1/tenants/tenant-a/alert-summary

缓存包装器应记录 Redis 读取警告日志，并继续进行 PostgreSQL 聚合。响应应报告 REAL_TIME_BACKFILL。由于 Redis 不可用，尝试回填也会记录一条警告，但当前 API 响应仍应正常返回。

在 Redis 保持停止状态时，多次调用该端点。因为没有可用的共享缓存值，每个请求都会从 PostgreSQL 中聚合数据。这演示了在较大系统中故障降级必须保持有限（bounded）的原因。Redis 宕机会将读取压力转移给 PostgreSQL。

重启 Redis：

docker compose start redis

等待它变为健康状态：

docker compose ps

调用该端点一次。如果键未被保留或已过期，应用程序将执行实时聚合，并将数据回填给 Redis。接下来的调用应该就会使用 CACHE。

如果应用程序在重启后的一小段时间内报告 Redis 连接错误，请等待几秒钟让连接工厂（connection factory）重新建立连接，然后重试请求。

import com.example.security.dto.AlertSummary;

class AlertAggregationServiceTest {

    void aggregatesSeverityAndOpenAlertCounts() {

        Clock clock = Clock.fixed(

            ZoneOffset.UTC
        );

第 15 步：调整本地开发配置

仅在调试时使用较短的缓存和调度间隔。一个实用的本地配置是两分钟的缓存 TTL 和 30 秒的调度延迟：

app:
  summary:
    cache-ttl: 2m
    schedule-delay-ms: 30000

这使得不用经历漫长等待就能观察到过期和刷新行为。这也意味着定时刷新通常会在键过期之前替换它。

使用比定时刷新间隔更长的缓存 TTL。如果调度器每五分钟运行一次，而 TTL 只有四分钟，那么键通常会在下一次定时刷新之前消失。这会产生不必要的缓存未命中。具有五分钟刷新间隔和十分钟 TTL，能提供一个简单的本地缓冲余地。

保持较短的 Redis 超时。Redis 是一条快速通道。一秒的超时对于本地机器来说已经足够宽裕。如果 Redis 不可用，应用程序应转入其降级（fallback）策略，而不是在重复且漫长的重试中等待。

本地开发时，保持较小的数据库连接池。对于本示例，10 个连接就足够了，这让偶然降级导致产生的压力更容易被观察到。过大的本地连接池会掩盖并发问题，直到部署到生产环境才爆发。

在调查聚合行为时，暂时启用 SQL 日志：

logging:
  level:
    org.hibernate.SQL: DEBUG
    org.hibernate.orm.jdbc.bind: TRACE

故障排查后，禁用详细的参数绑定日志，因为它会产生大量日志文件并可能暴露敏感的值。

在开发期间检查当前的 Redis 键：

docker exec -it security-redis redis-cli --scan \
  --pattern 'security:alert-summary:v1:*'

在重置缓存行为时，仅删除示例摘要的键：

docker exec -it security-redis redis-cli --scan \
  --pattern 'security:alert-summary:v1:*' | \
  xargs -r docker exec -i security-redis redis-cli DEL

当 Redis 与不相关的本地项目共享时，避免使用 FLUSHALL。

检查 PostgreSQL 查询行为：

docker exec -it security-postgres \
  psql -U security_user -d security_ops \
  -c "EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT severity, COUNT(*) FROM security_alert WHERE tenant_id = 'tenant-a' AND detected_at >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '24 hours' GROUP BY severity;"

随着数据集不断增加，该查询应使用租户和时间索引。由于种子行数极少，PostgreSQL 可能会选择顺序扫描，因为成本更低，这对于小型的本地数据集是正常现象。

完整的本地流程非常直观。定时处理能在需求到来之前预先计算共享摘要。Redis 服务常规请求路径。键缺失会触发实时 PostgreSQL 聚合。成功的结果将返回并回填入 Redis。之后的请求会重用那个缓存结果，直到下一次定时刷新、手动刷新、被逐出或过期。

title: Cloud Storage Pricing in 2026: What a Terabyte Actually Costs
description:
Cloud storage is sold by the month and marketed by the gigabyte, which makes five near-identical products look incomparable. Priced the honest way — dollars per terabyte per year, at the 2 TB tier most households actually buy — Google One and pCloud tie at $50.00, Dropbox and iCloud+ tie at $59.94, and Microsoft no longer sells a comparable solo tier at all.

The bigger story is what changed in 2026: Google folded its storage ladder into AI plans, and Microsoft quietly replaced its family's "1 TB each, up to 6 TB" with a single shared 2 TB pool.

Short version: For pure storage, Google One (sold as "Google AI Plus" at 2 TB) and pCloud's yearly plan are the cheapest subscriptions at $99.99/yr for 2 TB. iCloud+ costs 20% more for the same 2 TB but is the only big-name service with a free zero-knowledge encryption option. Microsoft 365 Personal is a fine Office bundle and a poor storage buy at $99.99 per TB. pCloud's lifetime deal still works, but a September 2026 price rise pushed its break-even point out to about five years.

At a glance

Google One iCloud+ OneDrive (M365) Dropbox pCloud
2 TB, per year $99.99 $119.88 — (no solo 2 TB) $119.88 $99.99
Cost per TB per year $50.00 $59.94 $99.99 (1 TB plan) $59.94 $50.00
Family model Shared pool, up to 6 people Shared pool, up to 6 people Shared 2 TB pool (new subs); was 1 TB × 6 Family plan: 2 TB shared, $203.88/yr Family is lifetime-only, from $749
Zero-knowledge encryption No Yes — Advanced Data Protection, free opt-in No No (consumer plans) Paid add-on, one folder only
Version history Trash: 30 days — Last 25 versions; full restore for subscribers 30 days on Plus 30 days (trash)
Watch out for Storage is now bundled into AI plans Monthly billing only — no annual discount Family storage cut for new subscribers Version history is shorter than rivals' Lifetime prices rose ~25% in Sept 2026

The per-terabyte table

Every plan below is the regular (non-promotional) US price, checked in November 2026. Where a vendor bills monthly only, we multiplied by twelve — because that is what you will actually pay in a year.

Plan Storage Monthly Per year $/TB/year
Google One Basic 100 GB $1.99 $19.99 $199.90
Google One Standard 200 GB $2.99 $29.99 $149.95
Google AI Plus (2 TB) 2 TB $9.99 $99.99 $50.00
Google AI Pro 5 TB $19.99 $199.99 $40.00
iCloud+ 50 GB $0.99 $11.88 $237.60
iCloud+ 200 GB $2.99 $35.88 $179.40
iCloud+ 2 TB $9.99 $119.88 $59.94
iCloud+ 6 TB $29.99 $359.88 $59.98
iCloud+ 12 TB $59.99 $719.88 $59.99
Microsoft 365 Basic 100 GB $1.99 $19.99 $199.90
Microsoft 365 Personal 1 TB $9.99 $99.99 $99.99
Microsoft 365 Family (new subs) 2 TB shared $12.99 $129.99 $65.00
Dropbox Plus 2 TB $9.99 billed yearly ($11.99 monthly) $119.88 $59.94
pCloud Premium 500 GB $4.99 $49.99 $99.98
pCloud Premium Plus 2 TB $9.99 $99.99 $50.00
pCloud Premium Plus, lifetime 2 TB — $499 once Break-even ≈ 5 years

Two patterns stand out. First, small tiers are terrible value everywhere: 100 GB costs about $200 per TB per year at both Google and Microsoft, four times the per-TB price of their 2 TB tiers. Second, iCloud+ has no volume curve at all — 2 TB, 6 TB and 12 TB all work out to roughly $60 per TB per year, because Apple bills monthly only and never discounts the big tiers.

A footnote: Box, once a storage staple, now caps its personal plans at 100 GB ($10/mo billed yearly), so it simply drops out of the terabyte conversation.

The five-year view

Per-year prices flatter subscriptions. Storage is something you keep for a decade, so here is the same 2 TB tier as a running total — and the one plan in this comparison that stops charging you.

Plan (2 TB) Per year 5 years 10 years
Google One (AI Plus) $99.99 $499.95 $999.90
pCloud Premium Plus (annual) $99.99 $499.95 $999.90
pCloud Premium Plus (lifetime) $499 once $499.00 $499.00
Dropbox Plus $119.88 $599.40 $1,198.80
iCloud+ $119.88 $599.40 $1,198.80
Microsoft 365 Family (2 TB shared) $129.99 $649.95 $1,299.90

The chart is also the honest case against over-reading it: the lifetime line only wins if pCloud is still operating, and still fits your life, in year six and beyond. That caveat gets its own paragraph below.

Three quiet changes in 2026

1. Google stopped selling plain storage. The public Google One page is now organised around AI plans. The mainstream 2 TB tier is sold as "Google AI Plus" ($99.99/yr) with Gemini usage limits bundled in, and the old AI Premium became "Google AI Pro" — renamed in 2025, then quietly upgraded from 2 TB to 5 TB in April 2026 at the same $19.99/mo, which makes it the cheapest subscription per terabyte ($40.00) if you can use 5 TB. Storage-only 5 TB and 10 TB tiers still exist for existing subscribers, but new buyers are funnelled to the AI bundles. The storage prices themselves ($1.99 / $2.99 / $9.99) have not risen in the US since launch.

2. Microsoft cut family storage by two-thirds. For a decade, Microsoft 365 Family meant 1 TB per person for up to six people — up to 6 TB in total. For new Family and Premium subscriptions started on or after October 8, 2026, Microsoft's own quota page now specifies a single 2 TB pool shared by everyone. Existing subscribers keep the per-person model until their renewal switches over, which Microsoft dates to May 2, 2027. If your household actually used those separate terabytes, the renewal letter matters more than the price: the price did not change, the product did.

3. pCloud's lifetime deal got more expensive. pCloud is the only major service still selling lifetime storage, and in September 2026 it raised every lifetime price by roughly a quarter: 2 TB went from $399 to $499. Against the $99.99 yearly plan, break-even moved from about four years to about five — still reachable, but no longer the obvious buy it was, and promotional pricing moves these numbers a lot (a mid-November promotion showed $379 for the same plan), so treat any lifetime figure as dated the day it is checked. "Lifetime" in pCloud's terms means the account holder's lifetime or 99 years, whichever is shorter.

The fine print cuts both ways. In pCloud's favour: there is no inactivity clause that deletes a dormant lifetime account, lifetime plans can be stacked (a 500 GB and a 2 TB plan combine), and purchases carry a 14-day money-back window. Against it: upgrades mean paying the full price of the added plan, the Crypto encryption add-on is never included, and a lifetime plan is ultimately a bet on the provider's longevity — the cautionary tale reviewers cite is Treasure Cloud, a lifetime storage service that shut down giving users 11 days to download their files. Five years to break even is short enough to be reasonable; it is not short enough to be risk-free.

One regional note: Apple raised iCloud+ prices in Japan and several other markets in July 2026 (in Japan, 2 TB went from ¥1,500 to ¥1,800 a month) while US prices stayed flat. If you are billed outside the US, your per-TB math may look worse than the table above.

Where the bill hides

Encryption is the real dividing line, and it is mostly absent. Of these five, only iCloud offers genuine zero-knowledge encryption: Advanced Data Protection is a free opt-in setting that extends end-to-end encryption to iCloud Drive, Photos and Backups. pCloud sells it as an add-on — Crypto, $49.99/yr or $150 lifetime — and it protects only the files you place in one special folder (a 2 TB lifetime plan with Crypto costs $649 once, not $499). Google One, OneDrive and consumer Dropbox offer no zero-knowledge option at any price; all three encrypt with keys the provider holds.

Version history is where Dropbox's cheap tier pinches. Dropbox Plus keeps only 30 days of file versions and deleted-file recovery — the 180-day window you may remember belongs to its professional tiers. OneDrive keeps the last 25 versions of a file, and Microsoft 365 subscribers can roll their whole OneDrive back to any point in the last 30 days. Google Drive's trash also empties after 30 days. If storage is your backup, the recovery window is part of the price.

Sync engines differ in ways that feel like price. Dropbox and Google Drive sync only the changed blocks of a file; OneDrive and iCloud lean on placeholder files that download on open. pCloud mounts a virtual drive but has no block-level sync, so editing a large file re-uploads the whole thing — a real cost on slow connections and metered plans. iCloud's Windows client remains the weakest of the group, which matters if your household is not all-Apple.

Family sharing is not the same product twice. Google and Apple share one pool with up to five other people at no extra cost, and each person's files stay private. Microsoft's new shared pool works the same way — but it replaced per-person terabytes, so heavy users now compete for the same 2 TB. Dropbox charges separately for family ($203.88/yr for the same 2 TB), and pCloud's family plans exist only as lifetime purchases.

Leaving has a price too, and it is paid in time. None of these services charges an egress fee to consumers, but the exits are not equal. Google Takeout splits exports into archives of at most 50 GB, delivered through download links that expire — a 2 TB library is forty archives and a weekend of babysitting. iCloud has no public file API, and full exports through Apple's privacy portal are prepared over days, not minutes. Dropbox and OneDrive let you sync everything down through the desktop client, which is slower than it sounds but at least continuous. None of this should decide your purchase; all of it should temper how "portable" you assume your archive is.

And the cheapest trick in this article: where annual billing exists, take it. Google One's annual plan is about 17% cheaper than paying monthly ($99.99 vs $119.88 a year), and Dropbox's is the same shape ($119.88 vs $143.88). iCloud+ offers no annual option at all — one more reason its effective price sits a tier above Google's.

Which one should you pick?

  • Pick Google One if you want the cheapest mainstream subscription and already live in Google Photos/Drive: 2 TB at $50.00/TB/yr, shareable with five people, and the 5 TB AI Pro tier is the best per-TB rate anywhere if you can fill it.
  • Pick iCloud+ if your photos and backups are Apple-shaped. You pay a 20% premium over Google for 2 TB and there is no annual discount, but Advanced Data Protection gives you the only free zero-knowledge option in this group.
  • Pick Microsoft 365 if you are really buying Office apps and Copilot — then the storage is a bonus. As a storage purchase alone, $99.99 for 1 TB is double Google's per-TB price, and families should check which storage model their subscription is on before renewing.
  • Pick Dropbox if sync speed and cross-platform reliability are the product for you. The per-TB price matches iCloud, but go in knowing Plus only keeps 30 days of versions.
  • Pick pCloud if you think in decades: the yearly plan ties Google at $50.00/TB/yr, and the $499 lifetime plan breaks even in about five years — provided you accept a smaller provider, no block-level sync, and extra cost for zero-knowledge encryption.

FAQ

What is the cheapest 2 TB cloud storage in 2026?
Google One (sold as Google AI Plus at this tier) and pCloud's Premium Plus tie at $99.99 per year — $50.00 per TB per year. Dropbox Plus and iCloud+ both cost $119.88 per year for 2 TB.

How much does 1 TB of cloud storage cost?
Almost nobody sells a standalone 1 TB tier. The exception is Microsoft 365 Personal at $99.99 per year — the same annual price as Google's 2 TB, for half the space, because you are really paying for the Office apps. If you need a terabyte, buy a 2 TB tier.

Is a lifetime cloud storage plan worth it?
pCloud's 2 TB lifetime plan costs $499 once, which breaks even against its own $99.99 yearly plan in about five years. It is worth it if you expect to keep the account well past that point and accept the risk that a smaller provider may not outlive a subscription at Google or Apple. Note that pCloud raised lifetime prices in September 2026 and runs promotions that undercut them, so the break-even moves with the price you actually pay.

Which cloud storage has end-to-end encryption?
iCloud, if you turn on Advanced Data Protection (free): it extends end-to-end encryption to Drive files, Photos and Backups. pCloud offers it only through the paid Crypto add-on, and only inside one folder. Google One, OneDrive and consumer Dropbox plans have no zero-knowledge option.

Why did my Microsoft 365 Family storage shrink?
For new subscriptions started on or after October 8, 2026, Microsoft replaced "1 TB per person for up to six people" with a single 2 TB pool shared by the whole family. Existing subscriptions keep the per-person model until renewal; Microsoft dates the switch-over for renewals to May 2, 2027.

How we checked: prices were read from the vendors' official pricing and help pages in November 2026 and cross-checked across independent pricing trackers. Google's plans page renders its prices inconsistently, so its figures were confirmed against the search-index cache of the same official page plus two trackers that read it on November 5, 2026; Microsoft's page was running a first-year promotion, so we list regular renewal prices; pCloud's lifetime prices change with promotions, so the $499 figure is a November 2026 check, not a promise. Vendors change pricing without notice; confirm before you buy. Full version with sources on SaaSPriced.

title: Executive Summary: Engineering Safe Database Fallback During Cache Failure
description:
Overview

A cache outage is not merely a latency issue; it is a massive load-transfer event. If a system natively routes all traffic to the database when a cache (like Redis) fails, the database will instantly become overwhelmed, turning a partial outage into a complete systemic failure. This document outlines the engineering principles required to safely manage database fallback through bounded concurrency, graceful degradation, and controlled recovery.

The Core Problem: The Load-Transfer Illusion

  • Asymmetric Capacity: Redis is designed to absorb massive, repeated read demand. The primary database is sized for writes, ingestion, and complex queries, not cache-level throughput.
  • The "Retry Storm": When Redis fails or slows down, naive fallback mechanisms dump 100% of the read load onto the database, compounded by users and automated clients aggressively retrying their delayed requests.
  • The Objective: Fallback must be treated as a scarce emergency resource. The goal is to preserve critical business functions (like active threat containment) while protecting the database, not to artificially maintain 100% feature availability.

Key Principles for Safe Database Fallback

1. Endpoint Classification and Graceful Degradation

  • Not all functions deserve emergency database access.
  • Critical endpoints (e.g., active incident status) receive reserved fallback capacity.
  • Important endpoints serve bounded stale data.
  • Deferrable endpoints (e.g., historical exports) fail fast (HTTP 503) to preserve resources.

2. Stale-While-Revalidate (The Safest Fallback)

  • The most efficient fallback query is the one that isn't executed.
  • Serve slightly expired data from a local, in-memory cache (like Caffeine) during transient Redis outages, explicitly labeling the data's age for the user so trust is maintained.

3. Bounded Fallback Concurrency (Bulkheads)

  • Implement strict concurrency limits (e.g., using semaphores). If the database can only safely handle 20 emergency read queries per second without disrupting core writes, any requests beyond that limit must be immediately rejected or served stale data.

4. Single-Flight Coordination

  • To prevent "cache stampedes" on missing popular keys, use single-flight controls. Only one request is allowed to execute the heavy database query, while simultaneous requests wait briefly to share the calculated result.

5. Prioritizing Authoritative Writes

  • During an outage, writing new security alerts and logging containment actions is more important than rendering monitoring dashboards. Read fallbacks must use isolated resource pools to prevent starving database writes.

Fast Detection and Controlled Recovery

  • Circuit Breakers: Use short timeouts and circuit breakers (e.g., Resilience4j) to detect Redis degradation instantly. Waiting seconds for a timeout consumes application threads and worsens the outage.
  • Controlled Rewarming: When Redis recovers, do not immediately dump all read traffic back to an empty cache. Systematically warm up high-value keys first to prevent a "cold-cache storm" against the database.
  • Observability: Monitor fallback permits in use, rejected emergency requests, and specific data freshness metrics, rather than relying solely on binary Redis process health checks.

title: async/await in practice: async code that reads like normal code
description:
This code looks right. It runs, it throws nothing, and the logs come out:

console.log("before");
[10, 20, 30].forEach(async (ms) => {
  await wait(ms);
  console.log("inside:", ms);
});
console.log("after");

before
after
inside: 10
inside: 20
inside: 30

And it's broken. forEach doesn't wait for async callbacks, so the code after it runs before the loop, and there's no way to know when the whole thing finished. No error, no warning: just a wrong order that in production becomes a response sent too early.

async/await solves the underlying problem — writing async code without chains of then — but it brings traps of its own. This lesson is about the three that hurt most.

An async function always returns a promise

async doesn't make a function magic: it changes its return type.

async function f() {
  return 1;
}

const p = f();
console.log(p);
console.log(p instanceof Promise);
p.then((value) => console.log("inside:", value));

Promise { 1 }
true
inside: 1

Whatever you return comes out as a promise. Return a value and the promise is fulfilled with it; throw and it's rejected. Which explains why .then works on an async function: it's just another promise.

await doesn't block, it suspends

The usual confusion is thinking await freezes the program. It freezes nothing: it suspends the current function and hands control back to whoever called it.

async function f() {
  console.log("a");
  await null;
  console.log("b");
}

f();
console.log("c");

a
c
b

await null isn't waiting for anything — null isn't a promise — and it suspends anyway. c runs before b because b sits in a microtask, which you already know from the event loop lesson.

If you come from Python, the syntax will feel familiar to the point of suspicion: async def, await, same shape. The difference isn't in the code, it's in the runtime. Python needs an event loop you start explicitly; Node already has one running. An await in Python without a loop is an error; in Node it's a Tuesday.

Sequential or parallel

This is where your endpoint takes 300 ms or 900. Three independent operations, 300 each:

const t0 = Date.now();
const [x, y, z] = await Promise.all([wait(300, "x"), wait(300, "y"), wait(300, "z")]);
console.log("parallel:", Date.now() - t0, "ms", x, y, z);

const t1 = Date.now();
const a = await wait(300, "x");
const b = await wait(300, "y");
const d = await wait(300, "z");
console.log("sequential:", Date.now() - t1, "ms", a, b, d);

parallel: 301 ms x y z
sequential: 901 ms x y z

The rule is easy to state and easy to forget: if an operation doesn't need the previous result, don't wait for it. Three awaits in a row mean "one after another", even when all three were independent.

And the detail that makes it pleasant: you can destructure the array Promise.all returns on the same line.

Top-level await, with small print

In an ES module you can use await at the top level, without wrapping it in a function:

const x = await Promise.resolve(1);
console.log(x);

1

But only in a module. The same code in a CommonJS file doesn't start:

const x = await Promise.resolve(1);
console.log(x);

SyntaxError: await is only valid in async functions and the top level bodies of modules

The message says it all. If your file is .js with "type": "commonjs", or .cjs, wrap the code in an async function and call it. Same reason import used to fail back in the modules lesson.

try/catch: the clean pattern

With async/await, error handling goes back to what it was before promises: try, catch, finally.

const fails = () => Promise.reject(new Error("the database is not answering"));

async function save() {
  try {
    await fails();
    console.log("this should not run");
  } catch (error) {
    console.log("recovered:", error.message);
  } finally {
    console.log("closing the transaction");
  }
  console.log("the function is still alive");
}
await save();

recovered: the database is not answering
closing the transaction
the function is still alive

await turns a rejection into an ordinary exception, and from there the catch you already knew works. No chained .catch, no error callbacks: the code reads top to bottom.

return await, or the catch that doesn't catch

There's a two-word difference that changes behaviour, and it's best seen by running it:

async function withoutAwait() {
  try {
    return Promise.reject(new Error("boom"));
  } catch (error) {
    return "caught: " + error.message;
  }
}

try {
  console.log("without await →", await withoutAwait());
} catch (error) {
  console.log("without await escaped:", error.message);
}

async function withAwait() {
  try {
    return await Promise.reject(new Error("boom"));
  } catch (error) {
    return "caught: " + error.message;
  }
}
console.log("with await →", await withAwait());

without await escaped: boom
with await → caught: boom

In the first one, return hands back the rejected promise without unwrapping it, so the inner catch never sees it and the error escapes to the caller. In the second, await unwraps it inside the try and the catch collects it.

The rule, with its exception: plain return is usually fine and return await is noise. The exception is exactly this one — when you return from inside a try that wants to catch the error — and then return await isn't optional.

When you forget the await

A rejection with no catch isn't a warning: it's an exception nobody collects, and Node won't let it slide.

async function save() {
  const result = Promise.reject(new Error("I forgot the await"));
  console.log("carried on without waiting");
}
save();

carried on without waiting
file:///tmp/l6/e.mjs:2
  const result = Promise.reject(new Error("I forgot the await"));
                                ^

Error: I forgot the await

And the process exits with code 1. The rest of the trace is the stack, which is beside the point here; what matters is that the rejected promise had nobody looking at it, and Node decided to stop pretending everything was fine.

It feels harsh. It's correct: an async error that gets ignored is an error that shows up later, somewhere else, in another shape — half a transaction, an incomplete record. Failing fast where the failure happened is cheaper than debugging its consequences.

The last resort: unhandledRejection

If you want to hear about those cases without the process dying at three in the morning, there's a global handler:

process.on("unhandledRejection", (error) => {
  console.log("last resort:", error.message);
});

async function save() {
  Promise.reject(new Error("I forgot the await"));
  console.log("carried on without waiting");
}
save();

carried on without waiting
last resort: I forgot the await

The process survives. Which is exactly why it should be used with care: it's a net, not a cushion. If the handler prints and moves on, you end up with a service that ignores its own failures and answers as if nothing happened. Its place is observability — telling someone who needs to know — not absolution.

Loops: for...of yes, forEach no

Back to the code from the start, now with the correct alternative. First the one that fails:

console.log("before");
[10, 20, 30].forEach(async (ms) => {
  await wait(ms);
  console.log("inside:", ms);
});
console.log("after");

before
after
inside: 10
inside: 20
inside: 30

And now the one that works:

console.log("before");
for (const ms of [10, 20, 30]) {
  await wait(ms);
  console.log("inside:", ms);
}
console.log("after");

before
inside: 10
inside: 20
inside: 30
after

for...of runs one iteration after another, and await works because you're genuinely inside an async function. forEach doesn't: it calls your callback, ignores what it returns and carries on. There's no way to await the whole loop, not even by putting await in front of it.

And if the order doesn't matter and you want parallelism, it's neither of those: it's Promise.all with a map.

const results = await Promise.all([10, 20, 30].map((ms) => wait(ms, ms)));
console.log("all at once:", results);

all at once: [ 10, 20, 30 ]

Three shapes, three behaviours: forEach doesn't wait, for...of waits in series, map with Promise.all waits in parallel.

And outside loops it's the same story

forEach isn't the only one ignoring what an async callback returns. setTimeout, an event handler, a server.on(...): none of them waits for your promise. If that promise rejects, nobody collects it.

setTimeout(async () => {
  throw new Error("nobody collects this");
}, 10);

Error: nobody collects this

And the process exits with code 1. The exception isn't seen by an outer try/catch or by setTimeout: it's an orphaned promise. When you write an async handler for an API that doesn't await callbacks, error handling is yours, inside the handler, always.

A timeout with Promise.race

Last piece: cutting off something that takes too long. Promise.race returns the first promise to settle, either way, and that's how you build a time limit.

const withTimeout = (promise, ms) => Promise.race([promise, wait(ms).then(() => Promise.reject(new Error("timeout")))]);

try {
  console.log(
    "slow:",
    await withTimeout(
      wait(500).then(() => "data"),
      100,
    ),
  );
} catch (error) {
  console.log("slow →", error.message);
}

try {
  console.log(
    "fast:",
    await withTimeout(
      wait(10).then(() => "data"),
      100,
    ),
  );
} catch (error) {
  console.log("fast →", error.message);
}

slow → timeout
fast: data

Whoever gets there first wins: if the data lands in 10 ms you get the data; if it takes 500 and the limit is 100, you get the timeout.

Mind what this doesn't do: it doesn't cancel the slow operation. The request is still alive in the background, burning a connection and memory; you've only stopped waiting for it. Real cancellation is a different thing, and it has a name.

Cancelling for real: AbortSignal

The standard way to interrupt something in JavaScript is an AbortController and its signal. The controller aborts; the signal is passed to the operation, which must have agreed to listen.

import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";

const control = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => control.abort(), 100);
const start = Date.now();

try {
  await sleep(1000, "done", { signal: control.signal });
  console.log("this should not run");
} catch (error) {
  console.log("aborted after", Date.now() - start, "ms ·", error.name);
}

aborted after 102 ms · AbortError

A hundred milliseconds in, the one-second timer stops waiting. The operation isn't cancelled by magic: the node:timers/promises API knows how to read { signal } and cuts out when the signal fires. If the API doesn't accept a signal, there's no cancellation, only patience.

For the most common case — a time limit — there's a shortcut that saves you the controller:

import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";

try {
  await sleep(1000, "done", { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(100) });
} catch (error) {
  console.log("built-in timeout ·", error.name);
}

built-in timeout · AbortError

And a third piece that saves manual checks: signal.throwIfAborted() throws the abort reason if it has already fired, carrying whatever reason you gave it. This is how file reads, fetch, streams and the in-flight work of a graceful shutdown get cancelled: the AbortController is passed down the stack and every layer checks its signal.

Common problems

The process dies with Error: ... and code 1 when I didn't throw anything

A rejection with no catch and no await. Look for the promise you created and never waited for: it's almost always a missing await.

forEach with async doesn't wait

That's what forEach does: it ignores the value the callback returns. Switch to for...of for series, or map with Promise.all for parallel.

My endpoint takes the sum of three calls

You're waiting for them one after another. If they're independent, they go in Promise.all.

Top-level await doesn't work in my file

It isn't an ES module. "type": "module" in package.json, a .mjs extension, or wrap it in an async function.

I added an unhandledRejection and now I don't see the errors

You're using it as a cushion. The handler should alert, not silence.

What you take from this lesson

  • An async function always returns a promise, carrying either the value or the error.
  • await suspends the current function, not the program.
  • If two operations are independent, they go in Promise.all: 300 ms, not 900.
  • Top-level await only exists in ES modules.
  • try/catch/finally is the error pattern again, with no chains of catch.
  • Forgetting an await kills the process, and rightly so: the error can't be lost.
  • unhandledRejection is an observability net, not forgiveness.
  • forEach doesn't wait; for...of waits in series; map with Promise.all in parallel.
  • Promise.race gives you a timeout, but it cancels nothing.

You can now write async code that reads. What's missing is the ground it lives on: the objects and modules Node gives you to talk to the system. The first is process, and with it the globals, the standard library and the pieces that are there without you importing them.

Never stop coding!
